tagline: From a narrow river canyon to aspen forest and Monte Cristo.
intro: Highway 39 leaves Ogden through a narrow quartzite gorge, then opens into a high valley at Pineview Reservoir near Huntsville. The canyon road has sharp curves; higher up, the route follows Beaver Creek into aspen forest. The Forest Service presents the Ogden River Scenic Byway in three parts: Ogden Canyon, Pineview Reservoir and the Monte Cristo road. Utah’s tourism office highlights the change from canyon to alpine country, with a high point near 9,000 feet.

Lorin Farr and Isaac Goodale built the first road through Ogden Canyon. A toll gate opened in 1860, and the Ogden Canyon Road Company operated it from 1865 until the road became public in 1882. The Ogden-Huntsville road joined the state highway system in 1911; in 1927 the legislature defined the road through to Woodruff as SR 39. In 1964, Ogden’s highway approach shifted north to 12th Street.

Drive east through the canyon to Pineview Dam, following the reservoir’s southern edge toward Huntsville. Beyond town, cottonwoods shade riverbank campgrounds before the road turns north along Beaver Creek and climbs toward Monte Cristo. The guard station and campground mark the byway’s end; the road continues thirty miles down to Woodruff in the Bear River Valley. The high crossing closes in winter.

moments.title: Ogden Canyon
moments.text: The Ogden River carved the canyon that carries Highway 39 east from the city. Quartzite forms the gorge, and the narrow road bends sharply beside the river. Much of the canyon is private property, with homes and businesses along it. Its first road was built by Lorin Farr and Isaac Goodale and charged tolls before becoming public in 1882. A lime kiln built in 1865 supplied mortar for pioneer construction; its restoration was completed in 2008. The canyon links Ogden at its western end with Pineview Dam at its eastern end, with smaller side canyons along the way.

moments.title: Pineview Reservoir
moments.text: Pineview Dam stands where the north, south and center forks of the Ogden River meet at the canyon’s eastern end. Increasing diversions had left irrigation water short in late summer, prompting a proposal for storage. The dam and Ogden-Brigham Canal were completed in June 1937 as part of the Ogden River Project. The later Weber Basin Project raised the dam from 103 to 137 feet, increasing storage capacity. SR 39 follows the water’s southern edge, while SR 158 crosses the dam. The reservoir was designed to provide dependable irrigation for land between the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake.

moments.title: Woodruff
moments.text: Woodruff lies at the foot of the thirty-mile continuation from Monte Cristo into the Bear River Valley. Settlers from what is now Bountiful arrived in 1870. The town took its name from Wilford Woodruff, fourth president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Its climate brings large differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures, including cold summer nights. Highway 39 ends here at Main Street, SR 16.

practical: Woodruff: The high road near Monte Cristo closes in winter, usually December through April depending on snow. Travel through Huntsville is year-round. (checked 2026-10-11)
